ai.description: This slender caecilian reaches 20–30 cm. It is dark brown to purplish-gray with a distinct reddish-pink tail tip. It possesses visible primary annuli and a terminal shield on the tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uraeotyphlus oxyurus* is best distinguished from other Indian caecilians by its distinctively pointed, conical snout and the presence of a true tail beyond the cloaca.
ai.habitat: The Red Caecilian inhabits moist, leaf-littered soils within tropical evergreen forests and plantations of the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 200 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Red Caecilian is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows at night to forage for earthworms and other small invertebrates in moist soil.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uraeotyphlus oxyurus* is oviparous, laying small clutches of terrestrial eggs in burrows. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, and females exhibit parental care.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uraeotyphlus oxyurus* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically inhabiting moist forests at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Red Caecilian produces a series of short, high-pitched clicks or chirps, typically heard from within moist soil or leaf litter near stream banks.
